RAZI-FULL:v21p171#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p171#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p171#2/r1.claim: The Quran describes God's breathing into Mary and into Adam; Razi notes that the wording concerning Jesus can grammatically refer to Mary because Jesus was in her womb.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The command for the angels to prostrate preceded Adam's creation; they were to prostrate after he was perfected and God's spirit was breathed into him.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: the directive given to the angels to prostrate before Adam (sws) was before he was created.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Human distinction rests on perfected abilities and the divine spark: preserving these merits the angels' prostration, while wasting them makes a person worse than an animal.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: if he wastes them, he is only an animal; in fact, even worse.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The divine spark is the source of spiritual advancement and connection with God when safeguarded; squandered, it leaves a person spiritually dark.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: It is this spark which is the fountainhead of all his spiritual advancements

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p476/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p476/r18.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p476/r18.claim: Sawwaytuhu means completing Adam's creation with precision and making its parts proportionate.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p476/r18.anchor: وسويته أكملت خلقه، والتسوية عبارة عن الإتقان، وجعل أجزائه مستوية فيما خلقت.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p476/r19.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p476/r19.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p476/r19.claim: “I breathed into him of My spirit” means God created life in Adam; no literal blowing or breathed object is intended, only a figurative image for imparting life.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p476/r19.anchor: ونفخت فيه من روحي أي: خلقت الحياة فيه، ولا نفخ هناك، ولا منفوخ حقيقة، وإنما هو تمثيل لتحصيل ما يحيي به فيه.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p476/r20.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p476/r20.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p476/r20.claim: The spirit is attributed to God as an honorific, like God's House and she-camel, or because God directly creates the spirit and places it where He wills.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p476/r20.anchor: وأضاف الروح إليه تعالى على سبيل التشريف نحو: بيت الله، وناقة الله، أو الملك إذ هو المتصرف في الإنشاء للروح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p476/r21.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p476/r21.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p476/r21.claim: The phrase waqaʿū lahu means that they fell to the ground.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p476/r21.anchor: وقعوا له أي: اسقطوا على الأرض.

STUDYQURAN:7:11/r16.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r16.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r16.claim: By focusing only on material origin, Iblis overlooks Adam’s ennoblement through God’s Hands, His Spirit, and exceptional knowledge.
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r16.anchor: Iblīs’s argument, based purely on the original substance from which Adam was created, makes Iblīs blind to other ways in which God had ennobled Adam

STUDYQURAN:15:intro/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:15:intro/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:15:intro/r7.claim: The rebellious Makkan idolaters are juxtaposed with Iblīs's refusal to bow to Adam after God created him.
STUDYQURAN:15:intro/r7.anchor: The rebelliousness of the Makkan idolaters in face of the truth is then juxtaposed with the refusal of Iblīs to bow before Adam

TABATABAI:15:26-48#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:26-48#3/r2.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
TABATABAI:15:26-48#3/r2.claim: A report says the spirit was created by God and breathed into Adam from it.
TABATABAI:15:26-48#3/r2.anchor: عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام قال سألته عن قول الله { ونفخت فيه من روحي } الآية قال روح خلقها الله فنفخ في آدم منها.

TABATABAI:15:26-48#3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:26-48#3/r3.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:15:26-48#3/r3.claim: God created a body and a spirit and ordered an angel to breathe into it; the spirit is from His power, not a part whose loss diminishes Him.
TABATABAI:15:26-48#3/r3.anchor: عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام في قوله { فإذا سويته ونفخت فيه من روحي } قال خلق خلقا وخلق روحا ثم أمر الملك فنفخ فيه

TABATABAI:15:26-48#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:26-48#3/r4.speaker: سماعة
TABATABAI:15:26-48#3/r4.claim: Sama'a transmits the Imam's account that Adam was created and breathed into, and that the spirit is God's power from the realm of malakut.
TABATABAI:15:26-48#3/r4.anchor: وفيه وفي رواية سماعة عنه عليه السلام خلق آدم ونفخ فيه. وسألته عن الروح قال هي قدرته من الملكوت.

TABATABAI:15:26-48#3/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:26-48#3/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:26-48#3/r5.claim: The spirit is God's active power, emanating from His essential power, as the preceding report indicates.
TABATABAI:15:26-48#3/r5.anchor: أي هي قدرته الفعلية منبعثة عن قدرته الذاتية صادرة منها كما يدل عليه الخبر السابق.

TABATABAI:15:26-48#3/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:26-48#3/r6.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
TABATABAI:15:26-48#3/r6.claim: The spirit is a specially chosen and created spirit, attributed to God and preferred over all spirits, from which He ordered Adam to be breathed.
TABATABAI:15:26-48#3/r6.anchor: سألت أبا جعفر عليه السلام عن قول الله عز وجل { ونفخت فيه من روحي } قال روح اختاره واصطفاه وخلقه وأضافه إلى نفسه

TABATABAI:15:26-48#3/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:26-48#3/r7.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
TABATABAI:15:26-48#3/r7.claim: In the report about Adam being created in God's image, the image is a created, originated form chosen above other forms and attributed to God as the Ka'ba is called His House.
TABATABAI:15:26-48#3/r7.anchor: وفي الكافي بإسناده عن محمد بن مسلم قال سألت أبا جعفر عليه السلام

TABATABAI:15:26-48#3/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:26-48#3/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:26-48#3/r8.claim: These are exceptionally valuable reports on the spirit and contain extensive teachings that will be explained when the nature of spirit is discussed.
TABATABAI:15:26-48#3/r8.anchor: وهذه الروايات من غرر الروايات في معنى الروح تتضمن معارف جمة وسنوضح معناها عند الكلام في حقيقة الروح إن شاء الله.

ASAD-NOTES:15:26/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:15:26/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:15:26/r1.claim: God forms mortal man fully, breathes spirit into him, and commands the angels to prostrate before him.
ASAD-NOTES:15:26/r1.anchor: when I have formed him fully and breathed into him of My spirit, fall down before him in prostration

ASAD-NOTES:15:26#n26/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:15:26#n26/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:15:26#n26/r1.claim: The creation and prostration passages are allegorical: God's creation requires no elapsed time, since His will brings a thing into being immediately, as several verses affirm.
ASAD-NOTES:15:26#n26/r1.anchor: the allegorical character of all the passages bearing on the creation of man and on God's command to the angels to prostrate themselves before him

ASAD-NOTES:15:26#n26/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:15:26#n26/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:15:26#n26/r2.claim: God's breathing of His spirit is a metaphor for endowing man with life and consciousness, that is, with a soul.
ASAD-NOTES:15:26#n26/r2.anchor: God's "breathing of His spirit" into man is obviously a metaphor for His endowing him with life and consciousness: that is, with a soul

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p23/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p23/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p23/r4.claim: Every command addressed to the angels in the Qur'an is masculine, as in اسجدوا, أنبئوني, and فقعوا له ساجدين.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p23/r4.anchor: كل فعل أمر يصدر إلى الملائكة يكون بالتذكير

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p669/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p669/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p669/r4.claim: The plural of majesty accompanies Mary’s conception through Gabriel, whereas Adam’s spirit was breathed directly after his creation and is phrased in the singular.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p669/r4.anchor: ومن الملاحظ في قصة مريم عليها السلام وعيسى - عليه السلام - أن الله تعالى جاء بضمير التعظيم

ALUSI-FULL:v14p36#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p36#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p36#2/r1.claim: Al-Ālūsī takes the making level as bringing Adam to balance and full readiness to receive the spirit.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p36#2/r1.anchor: فعلت فيه ما يصير به مستويا معتدلا مستعدا لفيضان الروح

ALUSI-FULL:v14p36#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p36#2/r2.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v14p36#2/r2.claim: An alternative explanation is that God formed Adam in human shape and the human constitution.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p36#2/r2.anchor: وقيل : صورته بالصور الإنسانية والخلقة البشرية

ALUSI-FULL:v14p36#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p36#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p36#2/r3.claim: In ordinary usage, blowing means sending air from the mouth or elsewhere into a cavity able to hold and fill with it.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p36#2/r3.anchor: النفخ في العرف إجراء الريح من الفم أو غيره في تجويف جسم صالح لإمساكها

ALUSI-FULL:v14p36#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p36#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p36#2/r4.claim: Here blowing figuratively represents imparting actual life to receptive matter; no literal blowing occurs.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p36#2/r4.anchor: والمراد هنا تمثيل إفاضة ما به الحياة بالفعل على المادة القابلة لها وليس هناك نفخ حقيقة

ALUSI-FULL:v14p36#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p36#2/r5.speaker: حجة الإسلام
ALUSI-FULL:v14p36#2/r5.claim: Al-Ghazālī explains the blowing image as a cause standing for its effect: prepared clay is like a wick ignited by fire, though the resulting life need not resemble the cause.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p36#2/r5.anchor: وقال حجة الإسلام : عبر بالنفخ الذي يكون سببا لاشتعال فتيلة القابل من الطين

ALUSI-FULL:v14p36#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p36#2/r6.speaker: حجة الإسلام وجماعة من المحققين
ALUSI-FULL:v14p36#2/r6.claim: Al-Ghazālī and other verificationists describe the spirit as an immaterial substance, neither body nor bodily accident, and neither inside nor outside the body or joined to it or separate from it.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p36#2/r6.anchor: ثم هذا الروح عنده وكذا عند جماعة من المحققين ليس بجسم يحل البدن

ALUSI-FULL:v14p36#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p36#2/r7.speaker: جماعة من المحققين
ALUSI-FULL:v14p36#2/r7.claim: Their first proof says universal intelligible forms cannot inhere in a point, which would always be receptive and make every point-bearing body rational, or in divisible matter, which would divide the forms.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p36#2/r7.anchor: وكذا عند جماعة من المحققين ليس بجسم يحل البدن

ALUSI-FULL:v14p36#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p36#2/r8.speaker: الشيخ
ALUSI-FULL:v14p36#2/r8.claim: The Sheikh's self-knowledge proof says self-awareness cannot depend on a second equal image, which duplicates the self; direct presence to oneself instead implies a self-subsisting, nonbodily intellect.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p36#2/r8.anchor: والدليل الثاني : ما عول عليه الشيخ وزعم أنه أجل ما عنده في هذا الباب

ALUSI-FULL:v14p36#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p36#2/r9.speaker: أفلاطون
ALUSI-FULL:v14p36#2/r9.claim: Plato argues that the mind can distinguish imagined nonexistent forms; the small body cannot contain these vast forms, and surrounding air is neither part of the body nor an instrument of the soul.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p36#2/r9.anchor: أفلاطون وهو أنا نتخيل صورا لا وجود لها في الخارج

ALUSI-FULL:v14p37/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p37/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p37/r1.claim: A fourth proof argues that if perceptions inhered in a body, one part could know while another part was ignorant of the same thing at the same time.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p37/r1.anchor: الدليل الرابع : لو كان محل الإدراكات شيئا جسمانيا لصح أن يقوم ببعض ذلك الجسم علم

ALUSI-FULL:v14p37/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p37/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p37/r2.claim: A fifth proof rejects an embodied soul: it would always perceive its organ, never perceive it, or perceive it only sometimes; each fails, and an image of the organ would either duplicate itself or require an immaterial soul.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p37/r2.anchor: الدليل الخامس : أن الروح لو كان منطبعا في جسم مثل قلب أو دماغ

ALUSI-FULL:v14p37/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p37/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p37/r3.claim: Al-Ālūsī says the Imam's al-Mabāḥith presents twelve proofs, including arguments already given, then relies on a further argument.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p37/r3.anchor: وقد ذكر الإمام في المباحث من الأدلة اثني عشر دليلا

ALUSI-FULL:v14p37/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p37/r4.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v14p37/r4.claim: The Imam's favored argument starts from our self-evident awareness that we are the same person as before: the self is neither the changing body nor an accident dependent on it, so it is an immaterial substance.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p37/r4.anchor: وقد ذكر الإمام في المباحث من الأدلة اثني عشر دليلا

ALUSI-FULL:v14p37/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p37/r5.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v14p37/r5.claim: He adds that animals may know their own identities, but do not know that their present selves are those that existed earlier, so the immaterial human self need not belong to every animal.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p37/r5.anchor: ولا يلزم أن يكون لسائر الحيوانات هذا الجوهر

ALUSI-FULL:v14p37/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p37/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p37/r6.claim: Al-Ālūsī introduces another proof: one entity in a person is the perceiver for every kind of perception and every object perceived.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p37/r6.anchor: قد دللنا على أن المدرك بجميع أصناف الإدراكات لجميع المدركات شيء واحد في نفس الإنسان

ALUSI-FULL:v14p38/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p38/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p38/r1.claim: The unified perceiver cannot be the body itself, a quality in every body part, or a quality in just one part: we do not find every part perceiving or one all-purpose perceiving organ.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p38/r1.anchor: فلو كان بعض الأجسام سواء كان جزأ من البدن أو محصورا في جزء منه موصوفا بالقوة المتعلقة بجميع هذه المدركات

ALUSI-FULL:v14p38/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p38/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p38/r2.claim: Nor can the perceiver be a subtle body hidden in an organ, since no such location is experienced; because we directly know ourselves as perceivers, an unknown body's identity cannot explain that self-awareness.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p38/r2.anchor: إنا قد دللنا على أنا السامعون المبصرون المتخيلون العاقلون

ALUSI-FULL:v14p38/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p38/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p38/r3.claim: These arguments conclude that the common subject of perception is neither body nor body-dependent, but an immaterial substance.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p38/r3.anchor: فثبت أن الموصوف بالقوة المدركة لجميع المدركات ليس جسما أصلا ولا قائما به

ALUSI-FULL:v14p38/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p38/r4.speaker: الذاهبون إلى التجرد
ALUSI-FULL:v14p38/r4.claim: Those who hold the spirit immaterial say its bond with the body resembles an instinctive, divinely inspired lover's attachment to the beloved and governs and directs the body while it remains receptive.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p38/r4.anchor: وذكر هؤلاء الذاهبون إلى التجرد أنه متعلق بالبدن كتعلق العاشق عشقا جبليا إلهاميا بالمعشوق

ALUSI-FULL:v14p38/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p38/r5.speaker: حجة الإسلام
ALUSI-FULL:v14p38/r5.claim: Al-Ghazālī says the possessive attribution 'My spirit' reflects creation without an intermediary that serves as origin or matter, or serves as an honorific attribution.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p38/r5.anchor: وإضافته إلى ضميره تعالى في الآية لأنه سبحانه وتعالى خلقه من غير واسطة

ALUSI-FULL:v14p38/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p38/r6.speaker: حجة الإسلام
ALUSI-FULL:v14p38/r6.claim: Al-Ghazālī compares this attribution to the sun saying it gave earth its light: the light is of the sun's kind, though extremely weak by comparison; the spirit's spacelessness and universal knowledge mark a likeness that warrants the attribution.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p38/r6.anchor: لو نطقت الشمس وقالت : أفضت على الأرض من نوري يكون ذلك صدقا

ALUSI-FULL:v14p38/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p38/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p38/r7.claim: Al-Ālūsī answers that two spaceless beings can remain distinct through their essences, just as different qualities in one body, or the same quality at different times, are distinct without separate places.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p38/r7.anchor: التميز غير منحصر بالمكان بل يكون به لجمسمين في مكانين وبالزمان

ALUSI-FULL:v14p38/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p38/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p38/r8.claim: He rejects the objection that being outside place is uniquely divine: God's unique attribute is self-subsistence, while everything else depends on and borrows its existence from Him.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p38/r8.anchor: وكون الوجود لا في مكان أخص صفاته سبحانه في حيز المنع بل الأخص أنه جل شأنه قيوم

ALUSI-FULL:v14p38/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p38/r9.speaker: المناوي
ALUSI-FULL:v14p38/r9.claim: Al-Munāwī says the factions' many rational speculations on the spirit yielded no sure result; Ibn Jamāʿa held that none of the more than a thousand views is sound.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p38/r9.anchor: قال الشيخ عبد الرؤف المناوي : قد خاض سائر الفرق غمرة الكلام في الروح فما ظفروا بطائل

ALUSI-FULL:v14p38/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p38/r10.speaker: جمهور أهل السنة
ALUSI-FULL:v14p38/r10.claim: The Sunni majority instead holds that the spirit is a subtle body differing from other bodies in essence and qualities, dwelling in the body like oil in olives or fire in coal; al-Juwaynī adopts this view.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p38/r10.anchor: وجمهور أهل السنة على أنها جسم لطيف يخالف الأجسام بالماهية والصفة

ALUSI-FULL:v14p38/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p38/r11.speaker: اللقاني
ALUSI-FULL:v14p38/r11.claim: Al-Laqqānī describes the spirit as a luminous, self-living, subtle upper body permeating the organs like rosewater in a rose; it does not decay, and its presence is life while separation is death.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p38/r11.anchor: وقال اللقاني : جمهور المتكلمين على أنها جسم مخالف بالماهية للجسم الذي تتولد منه الأعضاء

ALUSI-FULL:v14p39/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p39/r1.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v14p39/r1.claim: Some identify the human being with the visible bodily frame and make the spirit an accident inhering in it.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p39/r1.anchor: وزعم بعضهم أن الإنسان هو هذا الهيكل المحسوس وروحه عرض قائم به

ALUSI-FULL:v14p39/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p39/r2.speaker: بعض المتأخرين من المعاصرين
ALUSI-FULL:v14p39/r2.claim: Some later contemporaries ascribed that view to the majority of theologians and used it, together with the impossibility of uniting prior states, to argue that a servant does not create his own acts.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p39/r2.anchor: وعراه بعض المتأخرين من المعاصرين إلى جمهور المتكلمين وجعله وامتناع اتحاد القبل دليلا

ALUSI-FULL:v14p39/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p39/r3.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v14p39/r3.claim: The Imam rejects identifying the person with the visible frame and approves the majority position, since bodily parts continually change while the person remains the same from beginning to end.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p39/r3.anchor: رد الإمام في التفسير ذلك الزعم وارتضى ما نقلنا عن الجمهور

ALUSI-FULL:v14p39/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p39/r4.speaker: جمهور المتكلمين
ALUSI-FULL:v14p39/r4.claim: The majority reason that the enduring self cannot be the body, whose parts continually wither, grow, increase, diminish, mature, and dissolve; what changes completely is not the persistent person.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p39/r4.anchor: لا يجوز أن يكون الإنسان عبارة عن هذا الهيكل المحسوس لأن أجزاءه أبدا في الذبول والنمو والزيادة والنقصان

ALUSI-FULL:v14p39/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p39/r5.speaker: المحققون
ALUSI-FULL:v14p39/r5.claim: Among accounts of the self, the most satisfactory concise one says it consists of bodily components pervading the frame like water in a rose or oil in sesame; the discerning add that these components differ in nature from the frame's changing parts.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p39/r5.anchor: أن أسدها تحصيلا وتلخيصا أنها أجزاء جسمانية سارية في هذا الهيكل سريان الماء في الورد والدهن في السمسم

ALUSI-FULL:v14p39/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p39/r6.speaker: المحققون
ALUSI-FULL:v14p39/r6.claim: On this bodily-soul account, its own persistent particles are luminous and alive; they animate the changing frame, then separate at its corruption for the realm of holiness if blessed or afflictions if wretched.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p39/r6.anchor: ثم إن المحققين منهم قالوا أن الأجسام التي هي باقية من أول العمر إلى آخره

ALUSI-FULL:v14p39/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p39/r7.speaker: صاحب الهياكل
ALUSI-FULL:v14p39/r7.claim: The author of al-Hayākil argues that we never lose awareness of ourselves although we sometimes forget body parts; since a whole is known only through its parts, the self is beyond the body.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p39/r7.anchor: كلام صاحب الهياكل حسبما يدل عليه كلام شارحه الجلال حيث قال في الهيكل الثاني

ALUSI-FULL:v14p39/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p39/r8.speaker: الجلال
ALUSI-FULL:v14p39/r8.claim: Al-Jalāl objects that this proves only that the soul is beyond the visible body, not that it is immaterial; it could still be a subtle body.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p39/r8.anchor: وقال الجلال : فلا تكون النفس جسما أصلا لأن غاية ذلك إثبات أن النفس وراء هذا البدن

ALUSI-FULL:v14p39/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p39/r9.speaker: القاضي
ALUSI-FULL:v14p39/r9.claim: Al-Qāḍī says most theologians regard the spirit as an accident identical with life; Ustadh Abū Isḥāq adopts this despite the resulting accident-in-an-accident problem.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p39/r9.anchor: وزعم القاضي أن مذهب أكثر المتكلمين أن الروح عرض وأنها هي الحياة واختاره الأستاذ أبو إسحاق

ALUSI-FULL:v14p39/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p39/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p39/r10.claim: Al-Ālūsī answers that a spirit's being bodily does not make every body a spirit: it is spirit through a special divine property and is alive in itself, so no infinite regress of spirits follows.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p39/r10.anchor: فإنه إنما كان روحا لمعنى خصه الله تعالى به وقد علمت أن القائل بالجسمية يقول : إنه حي لذاته

ALUSI-FULL:v14p39/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p39/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p39/r11.claim: The animal spirit is a subtle vaporous body generated from subtle humors, arising from the heart's left cavity and spreading through the body as the rational soul's vehicle of control.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p39/r11.anchor: وعرفه في الهياكل بأنه جسم لطيف بخاري يتولد من لطائف الأخلاط وينبعث من التجويف الأيسر من القلب

ALUSI-FULL:v14p40/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p40/r1.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v14p40/r1.claim: Another account identifies the spirit with the balanced temperament of the heart's blood.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p40/r1.anchor: وقال بعضهم : إنه اعتدال مزاج دم القلب

ALUSI-FULL:v14p40/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p40/r2.speaker: بعض المحققين
ALUSI-FULL:v14p40/r2.claim: Some verificationists distinguish a subtle spirit permeating the body from a noble divine-command spirit that shines upon it and may give it life, perception, and luminosity.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p40/r2.anchor: وذهب بعض المحققين إلى أن الروح تطلق على الروح التي ذكر أنها جسم لطيف سار في البدن

ALUSI-FULL:v14p40/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p40/r3.speaker: بعض المحققين
ALUSI-FULL:v14p40/r3.claim: They take the spirit meant by the question in 17:85 to be the second, divine-command spirit.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p40/r3.anchor: ويعبر عنه بالروح الأمري وهو المراد من الروح في قوله تعالى : ( يسألونك عن الروح ) الآية

ALUSI-FULL:v14p40/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p40/r4.speaker: بعض المحققين
ALUSI-FULL:v14p40/r4.claim: In this terminology, the first spirit is the human self, while the second is the rational self; the immaterial substance described as neither body nor bodily is the spirit in this latter sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p40/r4.anchor: ويطلقون كثيرا على الروح بالمعنى الأول النفس الإنسانية وعليها بالمعنى الثاني النفس الناطقة

ALUSI-FULL:v14p40/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p40/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p40/r5.claim: Scholars disagree whether souls originate before or after bodies.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p40/r5.anchor: واختلفوا في أن حدوثها هل هو قبل الأبدان أو بعدها

ALUSI-FULL:v14p40/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p40/r6.speaker: حجة الإسلام
ALUSI-FULL:v14p40/r6.claim: Al-Ghazālī holds that souls arise when bodies become ready to receive them, like an image appearing when a mirror is polished, although the image's source existed earlier; Aristotle and his followers also held this.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p40/r6.anchor: فقال حجة الإسلام : الحق أن الأرواح حدثت عند استعداد الجسد للقبول كما حدثت الصورة في المرآة

ALUSI-FULL:v14p40/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p40/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p40/r7.claim: An objection cites a report that God created spirits two thousand years before bodies; no chain or grading is supplied here.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p40/r7.anchor: خبر أن الله تعالى خلق الأرواح قبل الأجسام بألفي عام

ALUSI-FULL:v14p40/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p40/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p40/r8.claim: Al-Ālūsī reports Ghazālī's answer that the spirits in this report are angels and the bodies are the world's vast bodies, such as the Throne, Kursī, and heavens, rather than human bodies.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p40/r8.anchor: لعل المراد من الأرواح في الخبر الأول الملائكة عليهم السلام وبالأجساد أجساد العالم من العرش والكرسي والسماوات

ALUSI-FULL:v14p40/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p40/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p40/r9.claim: The argument likens human spirits to a lamp kindled from an immense fire covering the world, the last spirit among the angels, and human bodies to the vastly larger cosmic bodies.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p40/r9.anchor: ولو انفتح عليك باب معرفة أرواح الملائكة لرأيت الأرواح البشرية كسراج اقتبس من نار عظيمة

ALUSI-FULL:v14p40/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p40/r10.speaker: حجة الإسلام
ALUSI-FULL:v14p40/r10.claim: His argument against preexistent souls says one soul shared by all would make everyone share the same knowledge and ignorance, while dividing one immaterial soul into many is impossible.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p40/r10.anchor: بأنها لو كانت موجودة قبل الأبدان فإما أن تكون واحدة أو كثيرة وعلى الأول إما أن تتكثر

ALUSI-FULL:v14p40/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p40/r11.speaker: حجة الإسلام
ALUSI-FULL:v14p40/r11.claim: If preexistent souls were already many, their individuation would require differences in essence, necessary properties, or accidents; shared species rules out the first two, while accidents cannot precede the body that supplies matter.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p40/r11.anchor: وعلى الثاني لابد أن يمتاز كل واحدة منها عن صاحبتها إما بالماهية أو لوازمها أو عوارضها

ALUSI-FULL:v14p41/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p41/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه الصلاة والسلام
ALUSI-FULL:v14p41/r1.claim: A Prophetic saying presents Muhammad as the first prophet in creation.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p41/r1.anchor: وأما قوله عليه الصلاة والسلام : أنا أول الأنبياء خلقا

ALUSI-FULL:v14p41/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p41/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه الصلاة والسلام
ALUSI-FULL:v14p41/r2.claim: Another Prophetic saying says Muhammad was a prophet while Adam was between water and clay.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p41/r2.anchor: وقوله عليه الصلاة والسلام : كنت نبيا وآدم بين الماء والطين

ALUSI-FULL:v14p41/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p41/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p41/r3.claim: The explanation reads “created” in the first-prophet report as predestination, not actual existence: ends precede their means in design but follow them in existence.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p41/r3.anchor: فالخلق فيه بمعنى التقدير دون الإيجاد فإنه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم قبل أن يولد لم يكن مخلوقا موجودا

ALUSI-FULL:v14p41/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p41/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p41/r4.claim: The architect's completed house is first as a design and last to exist; preparatory work serves it, just as first thought is last in the finished work.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p41/r4.anchor: فالدار الكاملة أول الأشياء في حق المهندس مثلا تقديرا وآخرها وجودا

ALUSI-FULL:v14p41/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p41/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p41/r5.claim: Human creation aims at knowing the happiness of nearness to God, attainable only through prophetic instruction; prophethood's completion in Muhammad is the goal, making him first in the plan and last in historical existence.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p41/r5.anchor: ولما كان المقصود من فطرة الآدميين إدراكهم لسعادة القرب من الحضرة الإلهية ولم يمكنهم ذلك إلا بتعريف الأنبياء

ALUSI-FULL:v14p41/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p41/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p41/r6.claim: The report about Adam is taken to indicate that Adam was made to yield the purest descendant, with selection continuing through generations until Muhammad.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p41/r6.anchor: وأنه لم يشأ سبحانه خلق آدم إلا لينتزع الصافي من ذريته ولم يزل يستصفي تدريجا إلى أن بلغ كمال الصفا

ALUSI-FULL:v14p41/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p41/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p41/r7.claim: The discussion distinguishes an ideal existence in the planner's mind from external existence; God's prior decree is inscribed on the Preserved Tablet before realization, as an architect's design precedes a house.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p41/r7.anchor: أن للدار مثلا وجودين وجودا في ذهن المهندس حتى كأنه ينظر إلى صورتها ووجودا خارج الذهن مسببا عن الوجود الأول

ALUSI-FULL:v14p41/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p41/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p41/r8.claim: The divine Pen conveys forms to the receptive Tablet according to eternal knowledge; neither need be physical, and they may be understood as spiritual teacher and learner.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p41/r8.anchor: واللوح عبارة عن موجود قابل لنقش الصور والقلم عبارة عن موجود منه تفيض الصور على اللوح

ALUSI-FULL:v14p41/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p41/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p41/r9.claim: The Pen and Tablet analogy is linked to 96:4, “He taught by the pen,” and the passage concludes that Muhammad preceded others in ideal existence, not actual existence.

ALUSI-FULL:v14p41/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p41/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p41/r10.claim: The first objection to the prior-soul proof asks why one preexistent soul could not later multiply; the reply distinguishes connected divisible unity from unity in general, since a universal affirmative does not convert.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p41/r10.anchor: الأول لم لا يجوز أن يقال : إنها كانت قبل الأبدان واحدة ثم تكثرت

ALUSI-FULL:v14p42/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p42/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p42/r1.claim: A second objection asks why multiple preexistent souls need distinct attributes: if attributes distinguish things, each attribute also needs distinguishing, producing circularity or infinite regress.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p42/r1.anchor: الثاني سلمنا أنها كانت متكثرة لكن لم قلتم لابد أن يختص كل بصفة مميزة

ALUSI-FULL:v14p42/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p42/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p42/r2.claim: A third objection says souls might differ by essential properties; the proof that they share one species does not establish that they must.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p42/r2.anchor: الثالث سلمنا أنه لابد من مميز فلم لا يجوز أن يكون بذاتي

ALUSI-FULL:v14p42/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p42/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p42/r3.claim: A fourth objection allows preexistent souls to differ through accidents caused by matter, proposing that each might have been attached to an earlier body, and so on; excluding this requires disproving transmigration.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p42/r3.anchor: الرابع سلمنا أنها لا تتميز بشيء من الذاتيات فلم لا يجوز أن تتميز بالعوارض

ALUSI-FULL:v14p42/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p42/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p42/r4.claim: The discussion says Ghazālī's proof of the soul's origination then depends on refuting transmigration, while philosophers use origination to reject it; the proposed chain leads to two souls in one body and circularity.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p42/r4.anchor: ولا مخلص من هذا إلا بإبطال التناسح فتوقف حجة إثبات حدوث الأرواح على ذلك الإبطال

ALUSI-FULL:v14p42/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p42/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p42/r5.claim: A fifth objection asks why, even without any previous body, souls could not differ by accidents, each caused by an earlier accident without a first one.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p42/r5.anchor: الخامس سلمنا عدم تعلقنا ببدن قبل لكن لم لا يجوز أن تكون موصوفة بعارض باعتباره كانت متميزة

ALUSI-FULL:v14p42#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p42#2/r1.speaker: المعترضون
ALUSI-FULL:v14p42#2/r1.claim: The objection says both camps hold souls survive bodily separation and are distinguished by accidents; for potential souls, attachment to different bodies may itself individuate them.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p42#2/r1.anchor: أن الأرواح عند الفريقين باقية بعد المفارقة ولا يكون تمايزها بالماهية ولوازمها بل بالعوارض

ALUSI-FULL:v14p42#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p42#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p42#2/r2.claim: If a soul divided, its parts would differ from the whole; essential difference makes the parts already distinct, while nonessential difference requires unequal magnitude and thus divisibility.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p42#2/r2.anchor: كل ما انقسم وجب أن يكون جزؤه مخالفا لكله ضرورة

ALUSI-FULL:v14p42#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p42#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p42#2/r3.claim: Even granting that an immaterial simple soul cannot split after unity, the individual determinations arise only after bodily attachment, so each soul is originated as an individual.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p42#2/r3.anchor: تعين كل واحدة من تلك النفوس من حيث هي حادثا وهو المطلوب

ALUSI-FULL:v14p42#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p42#2/r4.speaker: المعترضون
ALUSI-FULL:v14p42#2/r4.claim: An objection asks why distinction must depend on a qualifying attribute; Alusi answers by the same reasoning used for individuation itself.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p42#2/r4.anchor: الإمتياز لا يوجد إلا عند الإختصاص بوصف

ALUSI-FULL:v14p42#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p42#2/r5.speaker: المعترضون
ALUSI-FULL:v14p42#2/r5.claim: An objection proposes that souls differ through constitutive qualities; Alusi says it is not self-evident that each soul-kind must have several individuals, and one individual per kind would complete the argument.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p42#2/r5.anchor: إن النفوس لا يجوز أن تتمايز بالصفات المقومة

ALUSI-FULL:v14p42#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p42#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p42#2/r6.claim: The argument does not depend on disproving transmigration: plurality within one species shows individuality is not essential, but caused by relation to a particular body, so the soul is not individuated before that body.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p42#2/r6.anchor: ليس كذلك لأنا إذا وجدنا من النوع الواحد شخصين علمنا أن تلك الشخصية ليست معولة لتلك الماهية

ALUSI-FULL:v14p42#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p42#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p42#2/r7.claim: An inhering accident cannot distinguish a soul, since its inherence presupposes the soul is already distinguished; individuation must depend on the receptacle or body, while theologians also reject such accounts by infinite regress.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p42#2/r7.anchor: تلك العلة لا يمكن أن تكون حالة فيها لأن ذلك متوقف على امتيازها عن غيرها

ALUSI-FULL:v14p43/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p43/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p43/r1.claim: Potential souls first become distinct through attachment to particular receptacles; each then becomes aware of its own self, and that awareness persists, preserving distinction.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p43/r1.anchor: النفوس الهيولانية يتميز بعضها عن البعض أولا بسبب تعلقها بالقابل المعين ثم أنه يلزم من تعين كل واحد منها شعورها بذاتها الخاصة

ALUSI-FULL:v14p43/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p43/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p43/r2.claim: Before bodies, a soul could not be distinct: awareness follows distinction, and no other distinguisher exists to precede that awareness.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p43/r2.anchor: لو تميزت لكان المميز سوى الشعور حتى يترتب هو عليه وقد بين أنه ليس هناك مميز

ALUSI-FULL:v14p43/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p43/r3.speaker: صاحب المعتبر
ALUSI-FULL:v14p43/r3.claim: The author of al-Muʿtabar argues that prebodily souls either transmigrated from earlier bodies, which we would remember, or were idle in nature; Alusi calls the whole argument very weak.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p43/r3.anchor: استدل صاحب المعتبر على حدوثها بأنها لو كانت موجودة قبل الأبدان

ALUSI-FULL:v14p43/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p43/r4.speaker: قدماء الفلاسفة
ALUSI-FULL:v14p43/r4.claim: Ancient philosophers argue that anything originated needs matter to make existence preferable to nonexistence; thus an originated soul would be material, which they deny.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p43/r4.anchor: كل ما يحدث فلا بد أن يكون له مادة تكون سببا لأن يصير أولى بالوجود

ALUSI-FULL:v14p43/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p43/r5.speaker: قدماء الفلاسفة
ALUSI-FULL:v14p43/r5.claim: They argue that if souls began with bodies, infinitely many past bodies would entail infinitely many current souls, impossible because whatever admits increase and decrease is finite.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p43/r5.anchor: الثاني أنها لو كانت حادثة لكان حدوثها لحدوث الأبدان لكن الأبدان الماضية غير متناهية

ALUSI-FULL:v14p43/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p43/r6.speaker: قدماء الفلاسفة
ALUSI-FULL:v14p43/r6.claim: They argue that originated things perish, whereas souls are everlasting by consensus, so souls must be eternal.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p43/r6.anchor: أنها لو لم تكن أزلية لم تكن أبدية لما ثبت أن كل كائن فاسد

ALUSI-FULL:v14p43/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p43/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p43/r7.claim: Alusi accepts that souls depend for origination on bodies, but rejects the inference that dependence means they are bodily inhering in them.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p43/r7.anchor: ويرد عليهم أنه أريد بكونها مادية أن حدوثها يكون متوقفا على حدوث البدن فالأمر كذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v14p43/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p43/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p43/r8.claim: The claim that finite souls follow from their ability to increase or decrease is not self-evident and requires proof; the argument works only for things capable of bodily extension or inherence.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p43/r8.anchor: المقدمة القائلة إن كل قابل للزيادة والنقصان متناه ليست من الأوليات قطعا

ALUSI-FULL:v14p43/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p43/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p43/r9.claim: The philosophers give no proof for the premise that whatever is not eternal cannot be everlasting, so that premise is not accepted.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p43/r9.anchor: قضية لا حجة لهم على تصحيحها فلا تقبل

ALUSI-FULL:v14p43/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p43/r10.speaker: الغزالي والشيخ من الفلاسفة
ALUSI-FULL:v14p43/r10.claim: Al-Ghazali and the philosopher called the Shaykh hold souls are one species; Alusi says the Shaykh offered not even a doubt, much less a proof.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p43/r10.anchor: صرح به جماعة من المتكلمين كالغزالي وغيره وإليه ذهب الشيخ من الفلاسفة إلا أنه لم يأت لذلك بشبهة

ALUSI-FULL:v14p43/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p43/r11.speaker: غيره
ALUSI-FULL:v14p43/r11.claim: Another proponent argues that if human souls share their nature yet differ by an essential constituent, they would be composite and therefore bodily.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p43/r11.anchor: أن النفوس مشتركة في أنها نفوس بشرية فلو انفصل بعضها عن بعض بمقوم ذاتي

ALUSI-FULL:v14p44/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p44/r1.speaker: غيره
ALUSI-FULL:v14p44/r1.claim: A second argument for one soul-species says all people share capacities for knowledge and moral traits; since souls are known as perceiving and volitionally active, they are equal in all intelligible attributes.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p44/r1.anchor: الثاني أنا نرى الناس مشتركين في صحة العلم بالمعلومات وفي صحة التخلق بالأخلاق

ALUSI-FULL:v14p44/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p44/r2.speaker: غيره
ALUSI-FULL:v14p44/r2.claim: A third argument says every immaterial essence knows itself; Zayd's soul apprehends only an essence capable of cognition and volition, shared by all souls, so their full essence is one species.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p44/r2.anchor: نفس زيد مثلا مجردة فهي عاقلة لذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v14p44/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p44/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p44/r3.claim: Alusi rejects the first argument: souls might differ in species without sharing a genus, or share features as nonconstitutive concomitants; even essential composition need not be bodily.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p44/r3.anchor: لم لا يجوز أن هذه النفوس وإن كانت مختلفة بالنوع فهي غير متشاركة في الجنس

ALUSI-FULL:v14p45/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p45/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p45/r1.claim: The second same-species argument rests on inadequate induction: one cannot show every person receives every intelligible, or that a soul able to receive one attribute receives all attributes.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p45/r1.anchor: وأما الثاني فمداره الإستقراء ويضعف ذلك لوجهين

ALUSI-FULL:v14p45/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p45/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p45/r2.claim: The third argument would make all separate beings one species, which Alusi says is untenable.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p45/r2.anchor: يقتضي أن يكون جميع المفارقات نوعا واحدا وهو مما لا سبيل إليه

ALUSI-FULL:v14p45/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p45/r3.speaker: شرذمة وصاحب المعتبر
ALUSI-FULL:v14p45/r3.claim: A small group holds that souls differ by species, and this is the position of the author of al-Muʿtabar.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p45/r3.anchor: وذهب شرذمة إلى اختلافها بالنوع وهذا المعتبر عند صاحب المعتبر

ALUSI-FULL:v14p45/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p45/r4.speaker: صاحب المعتبر
ALUSI-FULL:v14p45/r4.claim: The best case for differing soul-species points to differences in knowledge, strength, anger, and forbearance despite similar temperaments, and prophetic power over universal matter not caused by temperament.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p45/r4.anchor: أحسن ما عول عليه في الإستدلال له اختلاف الناس في العلم والجهل والقوة والضعف

ALUSI-FULL:v14p45/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p45/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p45/r5.claim: Alusi says the argument from personal differences and prophetic power is not a proof, only weak persuasion.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p45/r5.anchor: ليس في الحقيقة من البراهين بل هو من الإقناعات الضعيفة

ALUSI-FULL:v14p45/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p45/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p45/r6.claim: The spirit's true nature is difficult to know; God made it a great sign of divine majesty and perfection.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p45/r6.anchor: أن الوقوف على حقيقة الروح أمر عسر والطويل إليه وعر وقد جعل الله سبحانه ذاك من أعظم آياته

ALUSI-FULL:v14p45/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p45/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p45/r7.claim: The angels' prostration to Adam may have been homage and honor, or prostration to God with Adam as the qibla where divine power's marvels appeared; Alusi cites Hassan's line about praying toward the qibla.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p45/r7.anchor: على وجه التحية والتعظيم أو لله تعالى وهو عليه السلام بمنزلة القبلة حيث ظهرت فيه تعاجيب آثار قدرته

ALUSI-FULL:v14p45/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p45/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p45/r8.claim: The command to fall down indicates actual prostration in its ordinary sense, not merely bowing as some suggested.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p45/r8.anchor: في أمرهم بالوقوع أي السقوط دليل على أن ليس المأمور به مجرد الإنحناء كما قيل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p380/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p380/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p380/r2.claim: Taswiyah means shaping Adam's form and completing his creation.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p380/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p380/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p380/r3.claim: The spirit is a subtle body by which humans live; it made Adam living, and its attribution to God is honorific.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p380/r3.anchor: {ونفخت فيه من روحي} فصار بشرا حيا، والروح جسم لطيف يحيا به الإنسان، وأضافه إلى نفسه تشريفا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p380/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p380/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p380/r4.claim: The commanded prostration was a greeting, not worship.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p380/r4.anchor: {فقعوا له ساجدين} سجود تحية لا سجود عبادة

BAYDAWI-FULL:15:28-29/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:15:28-29/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:15:28-29/r2.claim: To shape Adam is to proportion his form and prepare it for the spirit.
BAYDAWI-FULL:15:28-29/r2.anchor: { فإذا سويته } عدلت خلقته وهيأته لنفخ الروح فيه.

BAYDAWI-FULL:15:28-29/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:15:28-29/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:15:28-29/r3.claim: The spirit first attaches to subtle vapor from the heart, receives life, and travels through the arteries and body; its relation to the body is called blowing because air passes into another body’s cavity.
BAYDAWI-FULL:15:28-29/r3.anchor: وأصل النفخ إجراء الريح في تجويف جسم آخر، ولما كان الروح يتعلق أولا بالبخار اللطيف المنبعث من القلب

BAYDAWI-FULL:15:28-29/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:15:28-29/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:15:28-29/r4.claim: The spirit’s attribution to God follows the explanation given in al-Nisāʾ.
BAYDAWI-FULL:15:28-29/r4.anchor: وإضافة الروح إلى نفسه لما مر في «النساء».

BAYDAWI-FULL:15:28-29/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:15:28-29/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:15:28-29/r5.claim: Fa-qaʿū means fall down before him; it is the imperative of waqaʿa.
BAYDAWI-FULL:15:28-29/r5.anchor: فاسقطوا له. { سجدين } أمر من وقع يقع.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p220/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p220/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p220/r11.claim: God's fashioning means completing and adjusting Adam, preparing him almost fully for the imparting of spirit.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p220/r11.anchor: أي عدلته وأتممته وهيأته لنفخ الروح تهيئة قريبة من الفعل

BIQAI-FULL:v4p220/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p220/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p220/r12.claim: Breathing the spirit means creating life in Adam, figuratively like fire catching in a wick through blowing; attributing the spirit to God honors it, and its highest excellence is making a knower act humbly.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p220/r12.anchor: أي خلقت الحياة فيه كما تعلق النار بالفتيلة بالنفخ , وهو تمثيل

BIQAI-FULL:v4p220/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p220/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p220/r13.claim: The angels were commanded to prostrate in honor of Adam; falling as if involuntarily conveys their immediate and easy obedience.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p220/r13.anchor: اسجدوا له سجود من كان في مبادرته به وسهولة انقياده

BURSEVI:v4p305#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p305#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p305#2/r1.claim: Outwardly, God shaped Adam in human form; the breath means air entering a body able to retain it and is metaphor for creating life.
BURSEVI:v4p305#2/r1.anchor: أي صورته بالصورة الإنسانية والخلقة البشرية ونفخت فيه من روحي

BURSEVI:v4p305#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p305#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p305#2/r2.claim: There is no literal breath or breathed substance: the phrase describes the Creator’s relation to the created and manifestation of His attribute and act in Adam.
BURSEVI:v4p305#2/r2.anchor: ولا نفخ ثمة ولا منفوخ بل ليس عند الحقيقة

BURSEVI:v4p305#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p305#2/r3.speaker: الشيخ عز الدين
BURSEVI:v4p305#2/r3.claim: Shaykh ʿIzz al-Dīn says breath signifies ignition of the soul’s light in a receptive place; the physical image cannot apply to God, but its effect can be named for its cause.
BURSEVI:v4p305#2/r3.anchor: قال الشيخ عز الدين : النفخ عبارة عما اشعل نور الروح

BURSEVI:v4p305#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p305#2/r4.speaker: الشيخ عز الدين
BURSEVI:v4p305#2/r4.claim: For ʿIzz al-Dīn, the active cause is divine generosity, spring of existence and power, while the receiver is the balance created by shaping.
BURSEVI:v4p305#2/r4.anchor: قال الشيخ عز الدين : النفخ عبارة عما اشعل

BURSEVI:v4p305#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p305#2/r5.speaker: الشيخ عز الدين
BURSEVI:v4p305#2/r5.claim: He likens the receptive quality to a polished mirror that takes the image facing it; the soul appears when the embryo reaches balance.
BURSEVI:v4p305#2/r5.anchor: قال الشيخ عز الدين : النفخ عبارة عما اشعل

BURSEVI:v4p305#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p305#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p305#2/r6.claim: The Persian couplet compares the heart to a polished mirror capable of receiving limitless forms, and says polishers immediately see beauty.

BURSEVI:v4p305#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p305#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p305#2/r7.claim: God adds the breath to Himself because He personally shaped Adam with His holy hands and breathed directly, without intermediary.
BURSEVI:v4p305#2/r7.anchor: وإنما أضاف النفخ إلى ذاته لأنه تعالى باشر تسويته وتعديله فخلقه

BURSEVI:v4p305#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p305#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p305#2/r8.claim: The attributed spirit is the breath of the All-Merciful and shadowy existence, linked to 25:45.
BURSEVI:v4p305#2/r8.anchor: من روحه الإضافي وهو نفسه الرحماني الذي يقال له الوجود الظلي

BURSEVI:v4p305#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p305#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p305#2/r9.claim: This direct divine breath into Adam’s shaped form entails knowledge of all the Names, both gracious and majestic.
BURSEVI:v4p305#2/r9.anchor: نفخا استلزم لكونه نفخا بالذات فيما بوشرت تسويته باليدين معرفة الأسماء كلها

BURSEVI:v4p306#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p306#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p306#2/r1.claim: Faqaʿū is the imperative of waqaʿa and requires falling prostrate, not merely bowing, in obedience and as honor for Adam, who displays divine wonders like a qibla.
BURSEVI:v4p306#2/r1.anchor: أمر من وقع يقع وفيه دليل على أنه ليس المأمور به مجرد الانحناء

BURSEVI:v4p306#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p306#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p306#2/r2.claim: Bursevī recounts a true dream of his shaykh: he remained pure to his last breath, then performed ablution at a spring after death, ascended to heaven, and returned to pray at his own funeral.
BURSEVI:v4p306#2/r2.anchor: يقول الفقير : لي رؤيا صادقة في هذا المقام وهي أني رأيت حضرة شيخي

BURSEVI:v4p306#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p306#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p306#2/r3.claim: In the dream, the shaykh answers that earthly intellect and perception remain after death.
BURSEVI:v4p306#2/r3.anchor: فقلت له هل يبقى العقل والإدراك الذي في هذه النشأة الدنيوية على حاله

BURSEVI:v4p306#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p306#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p306#2/r4.claim: Bursevī infers that ablution is invalidated at death agony, grounding the sounder view that a deceased person must be washed; the complete believer remains pure, since hadath is not impurity.
BURSEVI:v4p306#2/r4.anchor: منها أن الوضوء ينتقض عند النزع وعليه بني مشروعية الغسل في الأصح

BURSEVI:v4p306#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p306#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p306#2/r5.claim: The complete person is washed as an imperfect person because outwardly he lacks ablution and follows the imperfect in worldly appearances.
BURSEVI:v4p306#2/r5.anchor: لأنه على غير وضوء بحسب الظاهر

BURSEVI:v4p306#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p306#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p306#2/r6.claim: Intellect, faith, sainthood, and similar qualities belong to the spirit and therefore do not change at death.
BURSEVI:v4p306#2/r6.anchor: لأن العقل والإيمان والولاية ونحوها من صفات الروح وهو لا يتغير بالموت

BURSEVI:v4p306#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p306#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p306#2/r7.claim: The perfected spirit’s funeral prayer signifies that in reality the perfected person is both prostrating and prostrated to; people’s prayer echoes angels’ prostration to Adam while remaining supplication at the legal level.
BURSEVI:v4p306#2/r7.anchor: فصلاته على نفسه إشارة إلى أن الكامل هو الساجد والمسجود له في مرتبة الحقيقة

BURSEVI:v4p307/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p307/r1.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v4p307/r1.claim: Al-Taʾwīlāt al-Najmiyya reads shaping as making Adam fit to receive the divine breath; the possessive spirit marks its special nearness and rank in the highest heavenly realm (50:16).
BURSEVI:v4p307/r1.anchor: قال في التأويلات النجمية : فإذا سويته تسوية تجعله قابلا لنفختي

BURSEVI:v4p307/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p307/r2.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v4p307/r2.claim: The spirit descends through angels, whose luminous qualities fold into it like starlight into sunlight; it then passes through jinn and devils, taking their traits, and through animals, receiving senses and powers.
BURSEVI:v4p307/r2.anchor: لأن الروح لما أرسل من أعلى مراتب القرب بنفخة الحق تعالى إلى أسفل سافلين

BURSEVI:v4p307/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p307/r3.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v4p307/r3.claim: The spirit attaches to Adam’s form, molded by God with gentleness and severity and prepared for manifestation; God commands prostration because of Adam’s perfected form, knowledge, and capacity for disclosure.
BURSEVI:v4p307/r3.anchor: ثم تعلق بالقالب المخلوق بيد الله المخمر فيه لطف الله وقهره المستعد لقبول التجلى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p43/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p43/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p43/r1.claim: The account of Adam is conjoined to another narrative; the opening idh is governed by an omitted 'remember,' as in parallel passages in al-Baqara and al-Aʿrāf.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p43/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p43/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p43/r4.claim: Specifying the human's material teaches that a creature's honor comes from its qualities, not the substance from which it is composed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p43/r4.anchor: وإنما ذكر للملائكة المادة التي منها خلق البشر ليعلموا أن شرف الموجودات بمزاياها لا بمادة تركيبها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p43/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p43/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p43/r5.claim: Taswiya is adjustment of a thing's constitution; here it is the balancing and completion of its elements until it can receive the spirit.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p43/r5.anchor: على اعتدال العناصر فيه واكتمالها بحيث صارت قابلة لنفخ الروح

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p43/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p43/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p43/r6.claim: Blowing literally expels compressed air between pursed lips; here it metaphorically denotes the sudden placement of a subtle, powerfully acting force, with no actual blowing or blown object.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p43/r6.anchor: استعير هنا لوضع قوة لطيفة السريان قوية التأثير دفعة واحدة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p43/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p43/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p43/r7.claim: As an approximation, life involves a rapidly formed vaporous or electrical force from the heart at the completion of bodily temperament, whose effects flow through arteries throughout the body.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p43/r7.anchor: وتقريب نفخ الروح في الحي أنه تكون القوة البخارية أو الكهربائية المنبعثة من القلب عند انتهاء استواء المزاج وتركيب أجزاء المزاج

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p43/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p43/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p43/r8.claim: Attributing the blowing and spirit to God's pronoun honors this creature.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p43/r8.anchor: وإسناد النفخ وإضافة الروح إلى ضمير اسم الجلالة تنويه بهذا المخلوق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p43/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p43/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p43/r9.claim: The passage implies that elements are distinguished before God by their effects and actions; human notions of dirtiness or purity reflect sensory response, temperament, or custom.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p43/r9.anchor: وفيه إيماء إلى أن حقائق العناصر عند الله تعالى لا تتفاضل إلا بتفاضل آثارها وأعمالها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p359#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p359#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p359#2/r5.claim: God announced an astonishing creation to angels made of light and subtle beings: He would make a living, bodily creature with skin from clay.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p359#2/r5.anchor: وأخبر الله تعالى الملائكة بعجب عندهم، وذلك أنهم كانوا مخلوقين من نور- فهي مخلوقات لطاف- فأخبرهم: أنه لا يخلق جسما حيا ذا بشرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p359#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p359#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p359#2/r7.claim: ‘I fashioned him’ means that God completed and perfected Adam until his parts were properly ordered.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p359#2/r7.anchor: وسويته معناه: كملته وأتقنته حتى استوت أجزاؤه على ما يجب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p359#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p359#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p359#2/r8.claim: The possessive phrase attributes a created, owned spirit to its Creator and Owner; ‘spirit’ here is a generic class term.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p359#2/r8.anchor: وقوله: من روحي إضافة خلق وملك إلى خالق مالك، أي من الروح الذي هو لي ولفظة الروح هنا للجنس.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p359#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p359#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p359#2/r9.claim: ‘Fall’ comes from waqaʿa/yqaʿu, with the qāf opened because of the following guttural letter.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p359#2/r9.anchor: وقوله: فقعوا من وقع يقع، وفتحت القاف لأجل حرف الحلق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p359#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p359#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p359#2/r10.claim: The verb supports the view that the angels’ prostration was the familiar physical act, not merely deference, submission, or a gesture.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p359#2/r10.anchor: وهذه اللفظة تقوي أن سجود الملائكة إنما كان على المعهود عندنا، لا أنه خضوع وتسليم، وإشارة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p359#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p359#2/r11.speaker: بعض الناس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p359#2/r11.claim: Some people explain the angels’ prostration as deference, submission, or a gesture rather than the familiar prostration; the author rejects this.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p359#2/r11.anchor: كما قال بعض الناس، وشبهوه بقول الشاعر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p359#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p359#2/r12.speaker: أبو الأخزر الحماني
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p359#2/r12.claim: Abū al-Akhzar al-Ḥammānī’s line says that a head ‘prostrated,’ a poetic parallel suggesting the familiar physical act.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p359#2/r12.anchor: وشبهوه بقول الشاعر [أبي الأخزر الحماني] : [الطويل] فكلتاهما خرت وأسجد رأسها ... كما سجدت نصرانة لم تحنف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p359#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p359#2/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p359#2/r13.claim: Al-Ṭabarī transmits from Ibn ʿAbbās that God created angels who refused Adam’s prostration and were burned, then created another group who obeyed except Iblīs, who was among the first.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p359#2/r13.anchor: وحكى الطبري في تفسير هذه الآية عن ابن عباس: أنه قال: خلق الله ملائكة أمرهم بالسجود لآدم فأبوا، فأرسل عليهم نارا فأحرقتهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p400/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p400/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p400/r1.claim: When God has fashioned Adam, He has proportioned his form and completed his creation.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p400/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p400/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p400/r2.claim: The spirit is the life-giving human spirit, whose nature is unknown; its attribution to God honors Adam and denotes ownership, and its entry is called breathing because it flows through the body like wind.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p400/r2.anchor: هذه الروح هي التي يحيا بها الإنسان ولا تعلم ما هيتها وإنما أضافها إليه تشريفا لآدم وهذه إضافة ملك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p400/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p400/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p400/r3.claim: Fa-qaʿū is an imperative form of the verb meaning to fall.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p400/r3.anchor: قوله تعالى ( فقعوا ) أمر من الوقوع

JISHUMI:v6p3945/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p3945/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p3945/r9.claim: Taswiya is setting things to an equal measure or form, and can also mean making them equal in judgment or another respect.
JISHUMI:v6p3945/r9.anchor: والتسوية: جعل كل واحد من الشيئين على مقدار الآخر، ثم يسوى بين الشيئين في الصورة

JISHUMI:v6p3945/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p3945/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p3945/r10.claim: Blowing is the act of sending air into something.
JISHUMI:v6p3945/r10.anchor: والنفخ: إجراء الريح في الشيء، نفخ ينفخ نفخا.

JISHUMI:v6p3946/r27.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p3946/r27.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p3946/r27.claim: One explanation says God completed Adam's creation and perfected him; another says He fashioned and completed his form.
JISHUMI:v6p3946/r27.anchor: بإتمام خلقه وكماله، وقيل: عدلت صورته وأكملت

JISHUMI:v6p3946/r28.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p3946/r28.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p3946/r28.claim: The blowing is a figurative expression for giving life; the spirit is attributed to God because He alone can do this, or as an honorific attribution.
JISHUMI:v6p3946/r28.anchor: كناية عن إحيائه، وأضافه إلى نفسه لأنه القادر عليه، وقيل: تشريفا وتعظيما

JISHUMI:v6p3946/r29.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p3946/r29.speaker: أبو القاسم
JISHUMI:v6p3946/r29.claim: Abū al-Qāsim says the prostration was a greeting, not worship; worship belongs to God, while the greeting was for Adam.
JISHUMI:v6p3946/r29.anchor: قيل: سجود تحية لا سجود عبادة، فالعبادة لله والتحية لآدم، عن أبي القاسم

JISHUMI:v6p3946/r30.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p3946/r30.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v6p3946/r30.claim: Abū ʿAlī says Adam was the direction toward which the angels prostrated, as the Kaaba is a direction of prayer.
JISHUMI:v6p3946/r30.anchor: وقيل: هو قبلة السجود كالكعبة، عن أبي علي

MUQATIL:15:29-31/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:15:29-31/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:15:29-31/r1.claim: God fashioned Adam's creation, breathed into him, and commanded the angels to prostrate to him.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p240#9/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p240#9/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p240#9/r1.claim: When God completed and formed Adam, He prepared him to receive the spirit.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p240#9/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p240#9/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p240#9/r2.claim: The spirit means that God gave Adam life; there was no literal blowing, which is figurative, and the possessive phrase marks special attribution.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p240#9/r2.anchor: وجعلت فيه الروح وأحييته وليس ثمت نفخ وإنما هو تمثيل والاضافة للتخصيص

NASAFI-FULL:v2p240#9/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p240#9/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p240#9/r3.claim: Waqaʿa means fall, here to prostrate; the fāʾ makes the command the answer to idhā, showing a command may precede its time of action.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p240#9/r3.anchor: هو أمر من وقع يقع أي اسقطوا على الأرض يعنى اسجدوا له ودخل الفاء لأنه جواب إذا

QURTUBI-FULL:15:28-29/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:15:28-29/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:15:28-29/r3.claim: I have proportioned it means that God formed and shaped Adam’s creation.
QURTUBI-FULL:15:28-29/r3.anchor: { فإذا سويته } أي سويت خلقه وصورته. { ونفخت فيه من روحي }

QURTUBI-FULL:15:28-29/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:15:28-29/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:15:28-29/r4.claim: Blowing means passing air into something.
QURTUBI-FULL:15:28-29/r4.anchor: النفخ إجراء الريح في الشيء. والروح جسم لطيف

QURTUBI-FULL:15:28-29/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:15:28-29/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:15:28-29/r5.claim: The spirit is a subtle body; God customarily creates life in the body together with it.
QURTUBI-FULL:15:28-29/r5.anchor: والروح جسم لطيف، أجرى الله العادة بأن يخلق الحياة في البدن مع ذلك الجسم.

QURTUBI-FULL:15:28-29/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:15:28-29/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:15:28-29/r6.claim: The spirit is a created thing attributed to its Creator for honor, like God’s earth, sky, house, camel, and month.
QURTUBI-FULL:15:28-29/r6.anchor: وحقيقته إضافة خلق إلى خالق فالروح خلق من خلقه أضافه إلى نفسه تشريفا وتكريما

QURTUBI-FULL:15:28-29/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:15:28-29/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:15:28-29/r7.claim: The phrase is comparable to روح منه in 4:171, explained earlier under al-Nisāʾ.
QURTUBI-FULL:15:28-29/r7.anchor: ومثله وروح منه [النساء: 171] وقد تقدم في «النساء» مبينا.

QURTUBI-FULL:15:28-29/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:15:28-29/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:15:28-29/r8.claim: In al-Tadhkira the author cited reports indicating that the spirit is a subtle body and that nafs and rūḥ name one referent; he plans to return to the subject.
QURTUBI-FULL:15:28-29/r8.anchor: وذكرنا في كتاب التذكرة الأحاديث الواردة التي تدل على أن الروح جسم لطيف، وأن النفس والروح اسمان لمسمى واحد.

QURTUBI-FULL:15:28-29/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:15:28-29/r9.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:15:28-29/r9.claim: Those who identify the spirit with life understand the phrase as meaning that God put life into Adam.
QURTUBI-FULL:15:28-29/r9.anchor: ومن قال إن الروح هو الحياة قال أراد: فإذا ركبت فيه الحياة.

QURTUBI-FULL:15:28-29/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:15:28-29/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:15:28-29/r10.claim: The command means to fall down prostrating to Adam.
QURTUBI-FULL:15:28-29/r10.anchor: { فقعوا له ساجدين } أي خروا له ساجدين. وهو سجود تحية وتكريم

QURTUBI-FULL:15:28-29/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:15:28-29/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:15:28-29/r11.claim: The angels’ prostration was greeting and honor, not worship; God may favor whom He wills and favored prophets over angels.
QURTUBI-FULL:15:28-29/r11.anchor: وهو سجود تحية وتكريم لا سجود عبادة. ولله أن يفضل من يريد ففضل الأنبياء على الملائكة.

QURTUBI-FULL:15:28-29/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:15:28-29/r12.speaker: القفال
QURTUBI-FULL:15:28-29/r12.claim: Al-Qaffāl says the angels were superior to Adam and God tested them by commanding prostration to him, exposing them to great reward; this is the Muʿtazilite position.
QURTUBI-FULL:15:28-29/r12.anchor: وقال القفال: كانوا أفضل من آدم، وامتحنهم الله بالسجود له تعريضا لهم للثواب الجزيل. وهو مذهب المعتزلة.

QURTUBI-FULL:15:28-29/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:15:28-29/r13.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:15:28-29/r13.claim: Another view says the angels were ordered to prostrate to God in Adam’s presence, with Adam serving as their qibla.
QURTUBI-FULL:15:28-29/r13.anchor: وقيل: أمروا بالسجود لله عند آدم، وكان آدم قبلة لهم.

RAZI-FULL:v19p144#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p144#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p144#2/r1.claim: After recounting the creation of the first human as evidence for a powerful, choosing God, the passage turns to God's command that the angels prostrate; all obeyed except Iblis.
RAZI-FULL:v19p144#2/r1.anchor: اعلم أنه تعالى لما ذكر حدوث الإنسان الأول واستدل بذكره على وجود الإله القادر المختار

RAZI-FULL:v19p144#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p144#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p144#2/r3.claim: One explanation of God's forming Adam is shaping him in human form and bodily constitution.
RAZI-FULL:v19p144#2/r3.anchor: الأول : فإذا سويت شكله بالصورة الإنسانية والخلقة البشرية .

RAZI-FULL:v19p144#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p144#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p144#2/r4.claim: A second explanation is arranging Adam's bodily parts through balanced temperaments and proportioned mixtures, as the verse about the human being formed from mixed fluid says.
RAZI-FULL:v19p144#2/r4.anchor: والثاني : فإذا سويت أجزاء بدنه باعتدال الطبائع وتناسب الأمشاج كما قال تعالى : { إنا خلقنا الإنسان من نطفة أمشاج }

RAZI-FULL:v19p144#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p144#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p144#3/r1.claim: Blowing is moving air through cavities in another body; the wording appears to imply that spirit is air, though the full account of spirit is deferred to 17:85.
RAZI-FULL:v19p144#3/r1.anchor: أن النفخ إجراء الريح في تجاويف جسم آخر ، وظاهر هذا اللفظ يشعر بأن الروح هي الريح

RAZI-FULL:v19p144#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p144#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p144#3/r2.claim: God attributes Adam's spirit to Himself as a mark of honor and distinction.
RAZI-FULL:v19p144#3/r2.anchor: وإنما أضاف الله سبحانه روح آدم إلى نفسه تشريفا له وتكريما

RAZI-FULL:v19p144#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p144#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p144#3/r3.claim: The exegetical question is whether the prostration was truly directed to Adam or whether Adam served as its qibla.
RAZI-FULL:v19p144#3/r3.anchor: أن ذلك السجود كان لآدم في الحقيقة أو كان آدم كالقبلة لذلك السجود

RAZI-FULL:v19p144#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p144#3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p144#3/r4.claim: The command may have addressed all heavenly angels, only some angels, or the angels of earth.
RAZI-FULL:v19p144#3/r4.anchor: أن المأمورين بالسجود لآدم عليه السلام كل ملائكة السموات أو بعضهم أو ملائكة الأرض

RAZI-FULL:v19p144#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p144#3/r5.speaker: بعض الناس
RAZI-FULL:v19p144#3/r5.claim: Some deny that the highest angels were commanded to prostrate to Adam, since the verse about those near God says they prostrate to God alone.
RAZI-FULL:v19p144#3/r5.anchor: من الناس من لا يجوز أن يقال : إن أكابر الملائكة كانوا مأمورين بالسجود لآدم عليه السلام

RAZI-FULL:v19p144#3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p144#3/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p144#3/r6.claim: The general wording commands prostration to Adam, but the specific statement that the angels prostrate to God alone takes precedence over that general wording.
RAZI-FULL:v19p144#3/r6.anchor: إلا أن الخاص مقدم على العام

RAZI-FULL:v19p144#3/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p144#3/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p144#3/r7.claim: The fāʾ in the command indicates immediate succession after God's forming and breathing the spirit, with no intervening delay.
RAZI-FULL:v19p144#3/r7.anchor: ظاهر الآية يدل على أنه تعالى كما نفخ الروح في آدم عليه السلام وجب على الملائكة أن يسجدوا له

STUDYQURAN:15:29/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:15:29/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:15:29/r1.claim: This verse repeats 38:72 and is compared with 32:9.
STUDYQURAN:15:29/r1.anchor: This verse is identical to 38:72; cf. 32:9

STUDYQURAN:15:29/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:15:29/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:15:29/r2.claim: God proportioned the human being by creating him in the most perfect manner to receive His Spirit, as in 95:4.
STUDYQURAN:15:29/r2.anchor: I have proportioned him is understood to be a reference to God’s creating the human being in the most perfect manner

STUDYQURAN:15:29/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:15:29/r3.speaker: many commentators
STUDYQURAN:15:29/r3.claim: Many commentators understand “My Spirit” as a reference to God's Power.
STUDYQURAN:15:29/r3.anchor: many commentators see My Spirit as a reference to God’s Power

STUDYQURAN:15:29/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:15:29/r4.speaker: other commentators
STUDYQURAN:15:29/r4.claim: Other commentators take the Spirit more literally as al-rūḥ, explaining why Iblīs was commanded to bow to Adam.
STUDYQURAN:15:29/r4.anchor: others take the phrase more literally as the Spirit

STUDYQURAN:15:29/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:15:29/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:15:29/r5.claim: The angels' prostration before Adam is essential to the Quran's creation account; it appears in several other passages.
STUDYQURAN:15:29/r5.anchor: God’s commanding the angels to bow before Adam is an essential part of the Quranic account of his creation

STUDYQURAN:15:29/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:15:29/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:15:29/r6.claim: One interpretation is that before their fall from Heaven, human beings held a station higher than the angels.
STUDYQURAN:15:29/r6.anchor: implies that before falling from Heaven, human beings occupied a station higher than that of the angels

STUDYQURAN:15:29/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:15:29/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:15:29/r7.claim: Alternatively, the angels prostrated to God while taking Adam as their qiblah, or direction of prayer.
STUDYQURAN:15:29/r7.anchor: or that the angels were bowing to God but taking Adam as their qiblah (i.e., the direction of prayer)

STUDYQURAN:15:29/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:15:29/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:15:29/r8.claim: Joseph's family also bows to him in 12:100, fulfilling the dream he had in 12:4.
STUDYQURAN:15:29/r8.anchor: where Joseph’s family bows down to him in fulfillment of his dream in 12:4

TAB-FULL:v14p66/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p66/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v14p66/r1.claim: God says that when He had formed and proportioned Adam and breathed life into him, Adam became a living human.
TAB-FULL:v14p66/r1.anchor: يقول: فإذا صورته فعدلت صورته {ونفخت فيه من روحي} [الحجر: 29] فصار بشرا حيا

TAB-FULL:v14p66/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p66/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v14p66/r2.claim: The angels' prostration was an act of greeting and honor, not worship.
TAB-FULL:v14p66/r2.anchor: سجود تحية وتكرمة لا سجود عبادة

TAB-FULL:v14p66/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p66/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v14p66/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that successive groups of angels refused to prostrate and were burned by fire; a later group obeyed, while Iblis remained among the earliest unbelievers.
TAB-FULL:v14p66/r3.anchor: حدثني جعفر بن مكرم، قال: ثنا أبو عاصم، قال: ثنا شبيب بن بشر، عن عكرمة، عن ابن عباس، قال: " لما خلق الله الملائكة قال: إني خالق بشرا من طين

SULAMI:v1p353#4/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p353#4/r1.speaker: أبو عثمان
SULAMI:v1p353#4/r1.claim: Abu Uthman says that after God distinguishes Adam through qualities of the spirit and repentance, the angels must stop disputing and submit to the command to prostrate.
SULAMI:v1p353#4/r1.anchor: قال أبو عثمان : فإذا خصصته بإظهار النعت عليه من خصائص

SULAMI:v1p353#4/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p353#4/r2.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p353#4/r2.claim: Al-Wasiti says Adam's knowledge, the spirit's knowledge, and its will are all constituted by God's knowing, knowledge, and willing; the spirit wills what God wills among its loves.
SULAMI:v1p353#4/r2.anchor: قال الواسطي : لما نفخ الروح في آدم جعل معرفتها معرفة الحق إياها

SULAMI:v1p353#4/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p353#4/r3.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p353#4/r3.claim: The angels first saw Adam's form but not the spirit's divine attribution, repentance, knowledge of names, or glimpse of the unseen; when God disclosed these marks of special friendship and nearness, they prostrated.
SULAMI:v1p353#4/r3.anchor: قال بعضهم : أبصرت الملائكة من آدم هيكله وشخصه

SULAMI:v1p353#4/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p353#4/r4.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p353#4/r4.claim: Al-Wasiti distinguishes Adam's spirit from other things by the completion of its form and the special divine attribution; it is brought near, enabled to know God's rule, effaced, and returned to God by indication.
SULAMI:v1p353#4/r4.anchor: قال الواسطي : الفرق بين روح آدم

SULAMI:v1p353#4/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p353#4/r5.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p353#4/r5.claim: The spirit is stripped of independent action and speech: it is adorned by God's creation, takes on His character, speaks through Him, and understands through His indication.
SULAMI:v1p353#4/r5.anchor: قال الواسطي : الفرق بين روح آدم

TABATABAI:15:28-29/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:28-29/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:28-29/r4.claim: Taswiyah means making something properly balanced and ordered, with each part in its proper place and condition; for a human, each organ is where and as it should be.
TABATABAI:15:28-29/r4.anchor: التسوية جعل الشيء مستويا قيما على أمره بحيث يكون كل جزء منه على ما ينبغي أن يكون عليه

TABATABAI:15:28-29/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:28-29/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:28-29/r5.claim: The wording suggests the first human's body was created gradually: first its parts were assembled, then arranged in their fitting places and states, and then the spirit was breathed into it.
TABATABAI:15:28-29/r5.anchor: أن خلق بدن الإنسان الأول كان على سبيل التدريج الزمانى فكان أولا الخلق وهو جمع الأجزاء ثم التسوية

TABATABAI:15:28-29/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:28-29/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:28-29/r6.claim: This gradual formation does not conflict with 3:59: its statement that God then said Be and it was concerns the soul's coming to be, not the body's formation.
TABATABAI:15:28-29/r6.anchor: فإن قوله { ثم قال له } الخ ناظر إلى كينونة الروح

TABATABAI:15:28-29/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:28-29/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:28-29/r7.claim: The author connects the body's gradual creation to 23:14, which describes the later creation of the human as another creation after the body was formed.
TABATABAI:15:28-29/r7.anchor: كما عبر عنه في موضع آخر بعد بيان خلق البدن بالتدريج بقوله ثم أنشأناه خلقا آخر

TABATABAI:15:28-29/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:28-29/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:28-29/r8.claim: Nafkh literally means putting air into a body through a mouth or otherwise, and can metaphorically mean imparting an intangible effect or command.
TABATABAI:15:28-29/r8.anchor: النفخ إدخال الهواء في داخل الأجسام بفم أو غيره ويكنى به عن إلقاء أثر أو أمر غير محسوس

TABATABAI:15:28-29/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:28-29/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:28-29/r9.claim: Here the blowing signifies God's bringing the human spirit into existence in its relation to and attachment to the body, not air literally entering it.
TABATABAI:15:28-29/r9.anchor: ويعني به في الآية إيجاده تعالى الروح الإنساني بما له

TABATABAI:15:29-33/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:29-33/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:29-33/r1.claim: Reading 23:13–14, the human spirit is the body brought into being as a new creation while the body itself remains unchanged.
TABATABAI:15:29-33/r1.anchor: فالآية الأولى - كما ترى - تبين أن الروح الإنساني هو البدن منشأ خلقا آخر والبدن على حاله من غير أن يزاد فيه شيء

TABATABAI:15:29-33/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:29-33/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:29-33/r2.claim: The spirit exists in itself, is united to the body through attachment, and is independent when that attachment ends at death; 32:11 says the spirit is taken while the body remains intact.
TABATABAI:15:29-33/r2.anchor: فالروح أمر موجود في نفسه له نوع اتحاد بالبدن بتعلقه به وله استقلال عن البدن إذا انقطع تعلقه به وفارقه

TABATABAI:15:29-33/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:15:29-33/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:15:29-33/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī points back to his discussion of the spirit at 2:154 and promises a fuller treatment at 17:85.
